stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.08 m has a total charge Q = +7 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 16 µF capacitor, a 80 kΩ resistor, an ideal 11 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.3 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.6 kg and length 0.3 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 1 Ω resistor. A uniform 0.7 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 6 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: An electron moves at $$4 \times 10^{6}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.08 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: A 3 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 3 µF and 1 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Not all the capacitors are in series.
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry 1 µC and 12 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.
The total is shared between two spheres.

questions.explanation: Total 13 µC, split equally: 6.5 µC each.

questions.stem: How much work must an external agent do to move a +7 µC charge slowly from a point at 131 V to a point at -50 V?
A battery with emf 15 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 9 Ω resistor. What is the current?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: A flat circular coil of 11 turns and radius 0.2 m carries 11 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: A wire 32 m long has a diameter of 2.2 mm and resistivity $$1 \times 10^{-7}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: A 16 µF capacitor is charged to 80 V. How much energy does it store?
Point P is 0.5 m from a +6 µC charge and 0.1 m from a −4 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: The negative charge contributes negative potential.
Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.

questions.stem: Two point charges of 8 µC and −1 µC are 0.16 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
A 0.1 m wire carrying 6 A makes a 90° angle with a uniform 0.1 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?
An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 150 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A 110-turn coil of area 0.11 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.3 T in 0.8 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries 17 A. What is the magnetic field 0.19 m from it?

options.why: A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.
That is the field at the center of a loop.

questions.stem: A solenoid 0.7 m long has 900 turns and carries 9 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.
Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 23 V and internal resistance 0.8 Ω is connected to a 20 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.
That is the internal voltage drop.
Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.

questions.stem: A 48 Ω resistor is connected across 45 V. What power does it dissipate?
A uniform field of 600 N/C passes through a flat 0.8 m² surface whose normal makes 60° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates 0.06 m apart have a potential difference of 190 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.04 m² separated by 7 mm, filled with a dielectric of κ = 2. What is its capacitance?
The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 9t$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s?
A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 9 µC/m. What is the field 0.2 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: An ideal 8 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 3 Ω resistor and a 0.5 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 0.0833$$ s?

options.why: Correct. τ = L/R = 0.167 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The current has not reached its final value.

questions.stem: A charge of +9q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 8$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.
Compare r², so take square roots.

questions.stem: A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.07 m has 5 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.182 m from its center?

options.why: Outside, all the charge is enclosed.
Correct. Outside, the sphere acts like a point charge.
Use the distance from the center, r.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 44 mH inductor and a 48 µF capacitor. What is its angular frequency ω of oscillation?
A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and remains connected to the battery. A dielectric with κ = 5 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's voltage?

options.why: Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. With the battery connected, V is fixed and C rises by κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. V fixed: Q = CV and U = ½CV² rise by κ.

questions.stem: A 9 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 8 Ω, connected to an ideal 9 V battery. What is the equivalent resistance?

options.why: Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.
R₂ and R₃ are in parallel.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.12 m carries 8 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.17 m from the center?

options.why: The charge is not at the center.
Only the axial components add; the others cancel.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 4 cm carrying 55 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 7 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
That is the larger sphere's charge.
Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 55: Q₁ = 20 nC.

questions.stem: A 0.2 m conducting rod slides at 12 m/s along rails connected by a 17 Ω resistor, perpendicular to a uniform 0.6 T field. What is the force needed to keep the rod moving at constant speed?

options.why: Correct. ε = BLv, I = ε/R, F = ILB = B²L²v/R.
That is the current; F = ILB.

questions.stem: Charges of +6 µC and +4 µC are 0.7 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 4.4 \times 10^{5} and 2.94 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 1.47 \times 10^{5} N/C.

questions.stem: Charges of -5 µC, -3 µC, -4 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.4 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.
Keep the signs of the charges.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 12 V battery and a 8 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 6 Ω and 5 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and remains connected to the battery. A dielectric with κ = 3 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's voltage?

options.why: Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Correct. With the battery connected, V is fixed and C rises by κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. V fixed: Q = CV and U = ½CV² rise by κ.

questions.stem: Charges of -2 µC, -4 µC, 5 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.4 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Keep the signs of the charges.
Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.05 m apart carry 14 A and 5 A in the same direction. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.
Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); parallel currents attract.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 40x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 1$$ m?
A 13 µF capacitor charged to 11 V discharges through a 20 kΩ resistor. What is the capacitor's voltage after 0.52 s?

options.why: Correct. τ = RC = 0.26 s; V = V₀e^(−t/τ).
Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
The change is exponential, not linear.

questions.stem: A rectangular loop of length 0.3 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 1 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.07 m and 0.16 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.04 m and at r = 0.16 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 9830 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
